summary.text: Maria Collett is a Democratic state senator who has represented Pennsylvania Senate District 12 in Montgomery County since December 2018 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026. A registered nurse and former deputy attorney general, she is the Senate Democratic Caucus Chair.

paragraphs.text: Maria Collett grew up in Maryland, according to her official biography, and holds a BA in English Literature from the University of Maryland at College Park, a JD from Rutgers University School of Law, and a BSN from Drexel University.

She worked as a Deputy Attorney General in Camden County, New Jersey, advocating for the rights of children, before moving into nursing, where she worked as a Level I trauma nurse, in pediatric home health, and in long-term care.
Collett ran for the Senate in 2018 and became the first Democrat elected to the seat, according to her biography.
In 2024, her Senate colleagues elected her Senate Democratic Caucus Chair.

She is the Democratic chair of the Aging and Youth Committee and serves on the Health and Human Services, Institutional Sustainability and Innovation, Judiciary, and Rules and Executive Nominations committees.

Her biography says she is the prime sponsor of the Family Care Act, which would establish a statewide paid family and medical leave program, and that she championed a 2021 Nursing Workforce Initiative that included a $55 million student loan relief program for nurses.
She lives in Lower Gwynedd Township with her husband, Len, and their son.
